comparisons.scheme2_value: Ensure universal access to basic banking services for unbanked households and individuals.

comparisons.scheme1_value: Single girl children only; merit-based (70%+ marks in class 10).
comparisons.scheme2_value: All Indian nationals, especially unbanked/low-income groups; minors 10+ years eligible.

comparisons.scheme1_value: Must study in CBSE-affiliated school; tuition fee ≤ Rs. 2,500/month (class 10) or ≤ Rs. 3,000/month (classes 11-12). NRI cap: Rs. 6,000/month.
70% or more marks in CBSE class 10 examination (mandatory).

Aadhaar, class 10 mark sheet, admission proof, student ID card, bank account details, fee receipt (school-verified), income affidavit on Rs. 50 stamp paper (attested by Gazetted Officer/SDM/First-Class Magistrate), passport-size photo, signature.
comparisons.scheme2_value: Aadhaar, Government ID (Voter Card/PAN/Ration Card), address proof (Passport/Driving Licence/utility bill), passport-size photo, filled PMJDY form, mobile number/email.
Offline at bank branch (form downloaded from pmjdy.gov.in).

recommendation:
These are two completely different schemes for different purposes:

**Choose CBSE SGC Scholarship if:** You are a single girl child, scored 70%+ in class 10, study in a CBSE school with capped fees, and need monthly financial aid for classes 11-12. Family income must be ≤ Rs. 8 lakh/year.

**Choose PMJDY if:** You or your family lacks a basic bank account and want free banking services, a debit card, and a small overdraft facility. This is not a scholarship—it's a financial inclusion tool.

**Overlap possibility:** You can apply for both if you meet eligibility. PMJDY provides banking; CBSE SGC provides scholarship support. Neither cancels the other.

**Next steps:** (1) Check CBSE scholarship page (cbse.gov.in/cbsenew/scholar.html) for current application windows and guidelines. (2) For PMJDY, visit your nearest bank branch or pmjdy.gov.in. (3) Consult your school principal or bank for specific questions.
